1574.text: A square loop $A B C D$, carrying a current $I_2$, is placed near and coplanar with a long straight conductor $X Y$ carrying a current $I_1$, as shown in figure. The net force on the loop will be
1574.sol:
Force on arm $A B$ due to current in conductor $X Y$ is
$F_1=\frac{\mu_0}{4 \pi} \frac{2 I_1 I_2 L}{(L / 2)}=\frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{\pi}$ acting towards the wire in the plane of loop.
Force on arm $C D$ due to current in conductor $X Y$ is
$F_2=\frac{\mu_0}{4 \pi} \frac{2 I_1 I_2 L}{(3 L / 2)}=\frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{3 \pi}$ away from the wire the plane of loop.
$\therefore \quad$ Net force on the loop $=F_1-F_2$
$=\frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{\pi}\left[1-\frac{1}{3}\right]=\frac{2}{3} \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{\pi}$

2147.text:
Assertion : One codon may code for more than one amino acid.
Reason: A codon is degenerate and ambiguous.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
2147.sol: The relationship between the sequence of amino acids in a polypeptide and nucleotide sequence of DNA or $m \mathrm{RNA}$ is called genetic code. The genetic code is triplet. One codon codes for only one amino acid, hence it is unambiguous and specific. Some amino acids are coded by more than one codon, hence the code is degenerate.

2799.text: Arrange the following in the correct order of their bond orders.
options: $I > I I > I I I > I V$
2799.sol:
Bond order is the number of chemical bonds present between two atoms of a molecule.
I. $\mathrm{N}_2=\sigma 1 s^2, \sigma^* 1 s^2, \sigma 2 s^2, \sigma^* 2 s^2, \pi 2 p_x^2=\pi 2 p_y^2, \sigma 2 p_z^2$ Bond order $=\frac{10-4}{2}=3$ II. $\mathrm{O}_2=\sigma 1 s^2, \sigma^* 1 s^2, \sigma 2 s^2, \sigma^* 2 s^2, \sigma 2 p_z^2, \pi 2 p_x^2\approx 2 p_y^2, \pi^* 2 p_x^1 \approx \pi^* 2 p_y^1$ Bond order $=\frac{10-6}{2}=2$ III. $\mathrm{O}_2^{+}=\sigma 1 s^2, \sigma^* 1 s^2, \sigma 2 s^2, \sigma^* 2 s^2, \sigma 2 p_z^2, \pi 2 p_x^2 \pi 2 p_y^2$,$\pi^* 2 p_x^1$ Bond order $=\frac{10-5}{2}=2.5$ IV. $\mathrm{O}_2^{-}=\sigma 1 s^2, \sigma^* 1 s^2, \sigma 2 s^2, \sigma^* 2 s^2, \sigma 2 p_z^2, \pi 2 p_x^2 \pi 2 p_y^2$,$\pi^* 2 p_x^2 \approx \pi^* 2 p_y^1$ Bond order $=\frac{10-7}{2}=1.5$ Hence, bond order can be arranged as I > III > II > IV

Find the observed EMF of the cell $\mathrm{Cd}\left|\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}(0.01 \mathrm{M})$\| $\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}(0.01 \mathrm{M})\right| \mathrm{Cd} \) under conditions, internal resistance of \(4 \Omega\) and producing a current of \(0.15 \mathrm{ A}\).

The cell representation is
\(\mathrm{Cd}/ \mathrm{Cd}^{2+}(0.01 \mathrm{M})\| \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}(0.01 \mathrm{M}) \mid \mathrm{Cu}\)

Q=$\frac{\left[\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}\right][\mathrm{Cu}]}{[\mathrm{Cd}]\left[\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}\right]}=\frac{0.01 \times 1}{1 \times 0.01}=1
\end{gathered}\)

& =[0.35-(-0.40)]-0 \quad[\because \log Q=\log \mathrm{l}=0] \\
& =0.75 \mathrm{ V}\\
\Rightarrow E_{\text{cell }^{\text{obscrved }} & =E_{\text{intemal }}-E_{\text{extemal }} \\
& =0.75-(\text{ resistance } \times \text{ current })\\
& =0.75-(4 \times0.15)=(0.75-0.60) \mathrm{V}\\
& =0.15 \mathrm{ V}
\end{aligned}$

3880.subject: Chemistry
3880.text: Which of the following sets is in the correct order regarding the property mentioned against them?
3880.sol:
I. Key Idea $(-I)$ group, if are present along with $-\mathrm{COOH}$ group in an acid, they increases the acidic property while (+) I groups or groups show hyperconjugation will decreases the acidic property. (a) $\mathrm{NCCH}_2 \mathrm{COOH}$ : Contain, $\mathrm{NC}$ (i.e. $-I$ ) group along with $-\mathrm{COOH}$, thus will increases the acidic nature. (b) $\mathrm{FCH}_2-\mathrm{COOH}$ : Contain, F (i.e. $-I$ ) group thus increases the acidic nature. Between $\mathrm{NCCH}_2 \mathrm{COOH}$ and $\mathrm{FCH}_2 \mathrm{COOH}, \mathrm{NCCH}_2 \mathrm{COOH}$ is more acidic due to stronger (-) $I$ effect. (c) $\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{CCH}_2 \mathrm{COOH}$ : Contain, $\mathrm{CH}_3$ group which show hyperconjugation effect and this is least acidic. Hence, the given order is correct. II) Key Idea (i) Structures which show more resonance structures or hyperconjugation among aldehydes are less reactive. (ii) Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones. a) $\mathrm{CH}_3 \cdot \mathrm{CH}_2 \cdot \mathrm{CHO}$ is an aldehyde in which $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-$ group show hyperconjugation effect.
reactive than $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CHO}$ due to resonance effect of Ph-group. Thus, correct order is $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \cdot \mathrm{CHO} > \mathrm{PhCHO} > \mathrm{PhCOCH}_3$ and the given order is not correct. (III) Key Idea Boiling point of alcohols (due to ability to form $\mathrm{H}$-bond) are higher than that of aldehydes which are more than that of ketones. (due to less steric-hinderance and more surface area in aldehyde group, having same number of C-atoms)
(c) $\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{OH}$ is an alcohol thus the given order for boiling point is correct. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

6904.subject: Mathematics
6904.text: A circle has its centre in the first quadrant and passes through $\left(2, 3\right)$. If this circle makes intercepts of length~$3$ and~$4$ respectively on $x = 2$~and $y = 3$, its equation is
6904.sol:
Consider a circle with centre be $\left(a, b\right)$.

So the equation of circle will be,

${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 2ax - 2by + c = 0 ⋯ \left(1\right)$

In the question it is given that the circle passes through $\left(2, 3\right)$.

Therefore, substituting $x = 2$ and $y = 3$ respectively in the equation $\left(1\right)$ we get,

${2}^{2} + {3}^{2} - 2a \times 2 - 2b \times 3 + c = 0$

$⇒ 13 - 4a - 6b + c = 0$

$∴ c = 4a + 6b - 13$

So now putting the value of $c$ in the equation $\left(1\right)$ we get,

${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 2ax - 2by + \left(4a + 6b - 13\right) = 0 ⋯ \left(2\right)$

Now we will find intercept on line $x = 2, y = 3$ respectivley.

By substituting $x = 2$ in the equation $\left(1\right)$ we get,

$4 + {y}^{2} - 4a - 2by + \left(4a + 6b - 13\right) = 0 ⋯ \left(3\right)$

In the equation $\left(3\right)$ let ${y}_{1}, {y}_{2}$ be the roots.

So, from equation $\left(3\right)$ sum of the roots will be,

${y}_{1} + {y}_{2} = 2b \ldots \left(4\right)$

Product of the roots will be,

${y}_{1}{y}_{2} = 6b - 9 ⋯ \left(5\right)$

Now as we know that length of intercept is $\left({y}_{1} - {y}_{2}\right)$. So we will use the identity, $a - b = \sqrt{{\left(a + b\right)}^{2} - 4ab}$

$⇒ {y}_{1} - {y}_{2} = \sqrt{{\left({y}_{1} + {y}_{2}\right)}^{2} - 4{y}_{1}{y}_{2}}$

$⇒ {3}^{2} = {\left({y}_{1} + {y}_{2}\right)}^{2} - 4{y}_{1}{y}_{2}$

Substituting the values of equation $\left(4\right)$ and $\left(5\right)$, we get

$⇒ 9 = {\left(2b\right)}^{2} - 4\left(6b - 9\right)$

$⇒ 4{b}^{2} - 24b + 27 = 0$

$⇒ 4{b}^{2} - 6b - 18b + 27 = 0$

$⇒ 2b\left(2b - 3\right) - 9\left(2b - 3\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(2b - 9\right)\left(2b - 3\right) = 0$

$⇒ b = \dfrac{9}{2}, b = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Hence the values of $b$ is $\dfrac{9}{2}$ or $\dfrac{3}{2}$

By substituting the value of $y = 3$ in the euqation $\left(2\right)$ we get,

${x}^{2} + 9 - 2ax - 6b + \left(4a + 6b - 13\right) = 0$

${x}^{2} - 2ax + 4a - 4 = 0 ⋯ \left(6\right)$

In equation $\left(6\right)$ let ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}$ be the roots,

Sum of the roots will be,

${x}_{1} + {x}_{2} = 2a ⋯ \left(7\right)$

Product of the roots will be

${x}_{1}{x}_{2} = \left(4a - 4\right) ⋯ \left(8\right)$

Again using same identity we get,

$\left({x}_{1} - {x}_{2}\right) = \sqrt{{\left({x}_{1} + {x}_{2}\right)}^{2} - 4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}}$

$⇒ 4 = {\left({x}_{1} + {x}_{2}\right)}^{2} - 4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}$

$⇒ 4 = {\left(2a\right)}^{2} - 4\left(4a - 4\right)$

$⇒ 4 = {a}^{2} - \left(4a - 4\right)$

$⇒ {a}^{2} - 4a = 0$

$⇒ a\left(a - 4\right) = 0$

Here the value of $a$ is $0$ or $4$.

So now there are $4$ such sets of equation can be made by the sets of vales of $\left(a, b\right)$ which are

$\left(0, \dfrac{3}{2}\right), \left(0, \dfrac{9}{2}\right), \left(4, \dfrac{3}{2}\right)$ and $\left(4, \dfrac{9}{2}\right)$.

For $\left(0, \dfrac{3}{2}\right)$ we will substitute in equation $\left(3\right)$, we get

${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 2ax - 2by + \left(4a + 6b - 13\right) = 0$

${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 2x\left(0\right) - 2y \times \dfrac{3}{2} + \left(4 ( 0 ) + 6 \times \dfrac{3}{2} - 13\right) = 0$

$∴ {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 3y + \left(- 4\right) = 0$

For $\left(0, \dfrac{9}{2}\right)$ we will substitue in equation $\left(3\right)$, we get

${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 2ax - 2by + \left(4a + 6b - 13\right) = 0$

${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 2x\left(0\right) - 2y \times \dfrac{9}{2} + \left(4\left(0\right) + 6 \times \dfrac{9}{2} - 13\right) = 0$

$∴ {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 9y + 14 = 0$

For $\left(4, \dfrac{3}{2}\right)$ we will substitue in euqation $\left(3\right)$, we get

${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 2ax - 2by + \left(4a + 6b - 13\right) = 0$

${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 2x\left(4\right) - 2y \times \dfrac{3}{2} + \left(4\left(4\right) + 6 \times \dfrac{3}{2} - 13\right) = 0$

$∴ {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 8x - 3y + 12 = 0$

For $\left(4, \dfrac{9}{2}\right)$ we will substitute in equation $\left(3\right)$, we get

${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 2ax - 2by + \left(4a + 6b - 13\right) = 0$

${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 2x\left(4\right) - 2y \times \dfrac{9}{2} + \left(4\left(4\right) + 6 \times \dfrac{9}{2} - 13\right) = 0$

$∴ {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 8x - 9y + 30 = 0$

So only ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 8x - 9y + 30 = 0$ is matching with the given option.

\left(x^2+y²-6 x-4 y+9\right) \text{ and } =0 \\
L:-2 x-2 y+14 \text{ and } =0 \Rightarrow L: x+y-7=0
\end{aligned} Check whether$(4,3)$ satisfy equation $L$.
LHS (4) + (3) $-7=0=$ RHS
\therefore x^2+y^2-6 x-4 y+9=0$ bisect the
circumference of circle $x^2+y^2-8 x-6 y+23=0$

8454.text: If $x=a$ is a root of multiplicity two of a polynomial equation $f(x)=0$, then
8454.sol:
Given that, $x=a$ is a root of multiplicity two of a polynomial equation $f(x)=0$.
Let $f(x)=(x-a) g(x)$
On differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get
$\Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x)=2(x-a) g(x)+(x-a)^2 g^{\prime}(x)$
Again, differentiating w.r.t $x$, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{ Now, } \begin{aligned}
& f^{\prime \prime}(x)=2 g(x)+2(x-a) g^{\prime}(x)+2(x-a) g^{\prime}(x) \\
&+(x-a)^2 g^{\prime \prime}(x)
\end{aligned} \\
& =2 g(x)+4(x-a) g^{\prime}(x)+(x-a)^2 g^{\prime \prime}(x)
\end{aligned}$
At $x=a$,
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad f^{\prime}(a)=2(a-a) g(a)+(a-a)^2 g^{\prime}(a)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad f^{\prime \prime}(a)=2 g(a)+4(a-a) g^{\prime}(a)+(a-a)^2 g^{\prime \prime}(a) \\
& \quad=2 g(a)
\end{aligned}$
Hence, $f(a)=f^{\prime}(a)=0, f^{\prime \prime}(a) \neq 0$

10754.subject: Mathematics
10754.text: Tom and Jerry play a game of alternately throwing an unfair coin. First one to get head wins. If Tom starts the game, he has $62. 5 %$ chance of winning the game. Suppose this coin is tossed $5$ times, then the probability of getting exactly $3$ heads is
10754.sol:
Tom and Jerry play a game of alternately throwing an unfair coin. First one to get head wins.

The coin is unfair, hence, let, the probability of getting a head when the coin is tossed is $x$ then the probability of getting a tail when the coin is tossed is $\left(1 - x\right) .$

If Tom starts the game, he has $62 . 5 % = \dfrac{62 . 5}{100} = \dfrac{5}{8}$ chance of winning the game.

He can win the game in first toss of the coin or second toss or third toss and so on means the cases are $H$ or $TTH$ or $TTTTH$ or $TTTTTTH$ and so on.

Thus, the probability of Tom winning the game is

$x + \left(1 - x\right) \times \left(1 - x\right) \times x + \left(1 - x\right) \times \left(1 - x\right) \times \left(1 - x\right) \times \left(1 - x\right) \times x + . . . = \dfrac{5}{8}$

$⇒ x + {\left(1 - x\right)}^{2}x + {\left(1 - x\right)}^{4}x + {\left(1 - x\right)}^{6}x + . . . = \dfrac{5}{8}$

Using the sum of infinite terms of a geometric progression i.e. $a + ar + a{r}^{2} + a{r}^{3} + . . . = \dfrac{a}{1 - r},$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{1 - {\left(1 - x\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{5}{8}$

$⇒ 8x = 5\left[1 - {\left(1 - x\right)}^{2}\right]$

$⇒ 8x = 5\left[1 - 1 + 2x - {x}^{2}\right]$

$⇒ 8x = 5\left[2x - {x}^{2}\right]$

$⇒ 8x = 10x - 5{x}^{2}$

$⇒ 5{x}^{2} - 2x = 0$

$⇒ x = 0$ or $x = \dfrac{2}{5} .$

But $x = 0$ is not possible, hence the probability of getting a head is $\dfrac{2}{5} .$

Now if this coin is tossed $5$ times, then the probability of getting exactly $3$ heads can be obtained by using Binomial distribution i.e.

$P\left(X = r\right) = Cr n {p}^{r}{q}^{n - r},$ where $n = 5, p = \dfrac{2}{5}, q = \dfrac{3}{5}, r = 3 .$

$P\left(X = 3\right) = C3 5 \cdot {\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right)}^{3} \cdot {\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ P\left(X = 3\right) = \left(\dfrac{5 !}{3 ! \times 2 !}\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{8}{125}\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{9}{25}\right)$

$⇒ P\left(X = 3\right) = \left(\dfrac{5 \times 4 \times 3 !}{3 ! \times 2 \times 1}\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{8}{125}\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{9}{25}\right)$

$⇒ P\left(X = 3\right) = \left(10\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{8}{125}\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{9}{25}\right) = \dfrac{144}{625} .$

15900.text: In the Uranium radioactive series, the initial nucleus is \({ }_{92}^{238} $\mathrm{U}$\) and final nucleus is \({ }_{82}^{206} $\mathrm{ Pb}$\). When the Uranium nucleus decays to lead, the number of \(\alpha\)-particles emitted is.......... and the number of \(\beta\)-particles emitted is ____.
15900.sol:
According to question,
Initial nuclei \(={ }_{92}^{238} $\mathrm{U}$\)
Final nuclei \(={ }_{82}^{206} $\mathrm{~Pb}$\)
Change in atomic number \(=92-82=10\)
When an \($\alpha$\)-particle emits from a nuclei, then its atomic number is decreased by 2 units and atomic mass is decreased by 4 units. When a \($\beta$\)-particle emits from a nuclei, then atomic number of parent nuclei is increased by 1 unit whereas its atomic mass remains same.
Change in atomic mass \(=238-206=32\)
Since, atomic mass changes only due to emission \($\alpha$\)-particle, hence number of emitted \($\alpha$\)-particle
\(=$\frac{32}{4}=$8\)
Number of emitted \($\beta$\)-particles = total change in atomic number due to emission of \($\alpha$\)-particles total change in atomic number
\(=8 $\times$2-10=6\)

20697.subject: Chemistry
20697.text: How many molecules of C$O_2$(g) are obtained on reaction of 24 grams of methane with 4moles of oxygen?
20697.sol:
The balanced chemical equation for the combustion of methane is:

$CH_4(g) + 2O_2(g) \rightarrow CO_2(g) + 2H_2O(l)$

Molar mass of $CH_4 = 16 \text{ g/mol}$

Moles of $CH_4 = \dfrac{24}{16} = 1.5 \text{ moles}$

Moles of $O_2$ given $= 4 \text{ moles}$

From the stoichiometry, $1 \text{ mole}$ of $CH_4$ requires $2 \text{ moles}$ of $O_2$. Thus, $1.5 \text{ moles}$ of $CH_4$ require $3 \text{ moles}$ of $O_2$. Since $4 \text{ moles}$ of $O_2$ are available, $CH_4$ is the limiting reagent.

Moles of $CO_2$ produced $=$ Moles of $CH_4$ reacted $= 1.5 \text{ moles}$

Number of molecules of $CO_2 = 1.5 \times N_A = 1.5 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 9.033 \times 10^{23}$

Answer: $9.033 \times 10^{23}$

20776.subject: Chemistry
20776.text: The electronic configuration of the element with atomic number 78 is:
20776.sol:
The atomic number of the element is $Z = 78$. This element is Platinum (Pt).

The noble gas preceding atomic number 78 is Xenon (Xe), which has an atomic number of 54.

The electronic configuration follows the Aufbau principle, filling the $6s$, $4f$, and $5d$ orbitals. The expected configuration based on the order of energy levels would be $[Xe] 4f^{14} 5d^8 6s^2$.

However, due to the stability associated with the filled $d$-subshell and the specific energy gaps between the $5d$ and $6s$ orbitals in heavy transition metals, Platinum exhibits an anomalous configuration where one electron from the $6s$ orbital is promoted to the $5d$ orbital.

Thus, the ground state electronic configuration of Platinum (Z = 78$) is $[Xe] 4f^{14} 5d^9 6s^1$.

Answer: $[X e] 4 f^{14} 5 d^9 6 s^1

21322.subject: Mathematics
21322.text: $Integrating factor of the differential equation \dfrac{d y}{d x}+y=\dfrac{x^3+y}{x}$ is
21322.sol:
The given differential equation is $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = \dfrac{x^3 + y}{x}$.

Rearranging the terms to the standard linear form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + P(x)y = Q(x)$, we have:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = x^2 + \dfrac{y}{x}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y - \dfrac{y}{x} = x^2$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{x}\right) = x^2$

Here, $P(x) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{x}$.

The integrating factor (IF) is given by $e^{\int P(x) dx}$.

IF $= e^{\int (1 - \dfrac{1}{x}) dx} = e^{x - \ln|x|} = e^x \cdot e^{-\ln|x|} = e^x \cdot \dfrac{1}{x} = \dfrac{e^x}{x}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{e^x}{x}$

21353.subject: Mathematics
21353.text: The sum of the degree and order of the following differential equation $\left[1-\left(\dfrac{d y}{d x}\right)^2\right]^{\dfrac{3}{2}}=k x \dfrac{d^2 y}{d x^2}$
21353.sol:
The given differential equation is $\left[1 - \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right]^{\dfrac{3}{2}} = kx \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$.

To determine the order and degree, the equation must be expressed as a polynomial in terms of the derivatives. Squaring both sides to eliminate the fractional exponent, we get:

$\left[1 - \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right]^3 = (kx)^2 \left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^2$.

The order of the differential equation is the highest derivative present, which is $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$. Thus, the order is 2.

The degree of the differential equation is the power of the highest order derivative when the equation is written as a polynomial in derivatives. Here, the power of $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ is 2. Thus, the degree is 2.

The sum of the degree and the order is $2 + 2 = 4$.

Answer: 4

21658.sol:
The given limit is $L = \lim_{x \rightarrow 0} \left( \dfrac{\sin ax}{\sin bx} \right)^k$.

We can rewrite the expression inside the limit as:

$\dfrac{\sin ax}{\sin bx} = \dfrac{\sin ax}{ax} \cdot \dfrac{bx}{\sin bx} \cdot \dfrac{ax}{bx}$

Using the standard limit $\lim_{\theta \rightarrow 0} \dfrac{\sin \theta}{\theta} = 1$, we have:

$\lim_{x \rightarrow 0} \dfrac{\sin ax}{ax} = 1$ and $\lim_{x \rightarrow 0} \dfrac{bx}{\sin bx} = 1$.

Therefore, $\lim_{x \rightarrow 0} \dfrac{\sin ax}{\sin bx} = \lim_{x \rightarrow 0} \left( \dfrac{\sin ax}{ax} \cdot \dfrac{bx}{\sin bx} \cdot \dfrac{a}{b} \right) = 1 \cdot 1 \cdot \dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{a}{b}$.

Applying the power $k$ to the limit:

$L = \left( \lim_{x \rightarrow 0} \dfrac{\sin ax}{\sin bx} \right)^k = \left( \dfrac{a}{b} \right)^k$.

Answer: $\left(\dfrac{a}{b}\right)^k$

21750.subject: Mathematics
21750.text: If $A=\left[\begin{array}{lll}2 & 1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{array}\right]$ and I is an identity by matrix of order $3 \times 3$ then $A(\operatorname{adj} A)=$
21750.sol:
The property of the adjoint of a matrix states that $A(\operatorname{adj} A) = |A| I$, where $|A|$ is the determinant of matrix $A$ and $I$ is the identity matrix of the same order.

Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$, we calculate the determinant $|A|$ by expanding along the first row:

$|A| = 2(1 \times 3 - 2 \times 2) - 1(3 \times 3 - 2 \times 1) + 3(3 \times 2 - 1 \times 1)$

$|A| = 2(3 - 4) - 1(9 - 2) + 3(6 - 1)$

$|A| = 2(-1) - 1(7) + 3(5)$

$|A| = -2 - 7 + 15 = 6$

Therefore, $A(\operatorname{adj} A) = 6I$.

Answer: 6 I

22172.text: If $Q(1,0,1)$ is the image of the point $P(a, b, c)$ in the line $\dfrac{x+1}{2}=\dfrac{y-3}{-2}=\dfrac{z}{-1}$ then $a+b+c$ is equal to
22172.sol:
Let the line be $L: \dfrac{x+1}{2} = \dfrac{y-3}{-2} = \dfrac{z}{-1} = k$. Any point $M$ on the line is given by $M(2k-1, -2k+3, -k)$.

Since $Q(1, 0, 1)$ is the image of $P(a, b, c)$ in the line, $M$ is the midpoint of $PQ$. Thus, $M = \left( \dfrac{a+1}{2}, \dfrac{b+0}{2}, \dfrac{c+1}{2} \right).

Equating the coordinates of $M$ with the parametric form:
\dfrac{a+1}{2} =$2k-1 \Rightarrow a = 4k-3$
\dfrac{b}{2} = -$2k+3 \Rightarrow b = -4k+6$
\dfrac{c+1}{2} = -$k \Rightarrow c = -2k-1$

The vector \overrightarrow{PQ} = (1-a, 0-b, 1-c) = (1-(4k-3), -( -4k+6), 1-(-2k-1)) = (4-4k, 4k-6, 2k+2)$ must be perpendicular to the direction vector of the line $\vec{v} = (2, -2, -1)$.

Therefore, \overrightarrow{PQ} \cdot $\vec{v} =$$0$:
$2(4-4k) - 2(4k-6) - 1(2k+2) = 0$
$8 - 8k - 8k + 12 - 2k - 2 = 0$
$-18k + 18 = 0 \Rightarrow k = 1$.

Substituting $k=1$ into the expressions for $a, b, c$:
$a = 4(1)-3 = 1$
$b = -4(1)+6 = 2$
$c = -2(1)-1 = -3$

The sum $a+b+c = 1 + 2 - 3 = 0$.

Answer: 0

23075.text: On both sides of a magnetic needle, two short magnets A and B are placed on the same horizontal line which is perpendicular to the magnetic meridian. The south poles of A and B are facing each other, which are 10 cm and 20 cm respectively from the magnetic needle. If the needle remains undeflected, the ratio of the magnetic moment of A to that B is:
23075.sol:
The magnetic field due to a short magnet on its axial line at a distance $d$ is given by $B = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \dfrac{2M}{d^3}$.

Since the magnetic needle remains undeflected, the magnetic fields produced by magnets A and B at the position of the needle must be equal and opposite.

$B_A = B_B$

$\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \dfrac{2M_A}{d_A^3} = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \dfrac{2M_B}{d_B^3}$

$\dfrac{M_A}{M_B} = \left(\dfrac{d_A}{d_B}\right)^3$

Given $d_A = 10\text{ cm}$ and $d_B = 20\text{ cm}$.

$\dfrac{M_A}{M_B} = \left(\dfrac{10}{20}\right)^3 = \dfrac{1}{8}$

The ratio of the magnetic moment of A to that of B is $1:8$.

Answer: $1:8$

23274.subject: Physics
23274.text: The closest approach of an alpha particle when it make a head on collision with a gold nucleus is $10 \times 10^{-14} \mathrm{ m}$, then the kinetic energy of the alpha particle is :
23274.sol:
The distance of closest approach $r_0$ for an alpha particle of kinetic energy $K$ colliding head-on with a nucleus of atomic number $Z$ is given by the conservation of energy:

$K = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_0} \dfrac{(Ze)(2e)}{r_0}$

For a gold nucleus, the atomic number $Z = 79$. The value of the Coulomb constant is $\dfrac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9 \text{ N m}^2 \text{ C}^{-2}$. The charge of an electron is $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$.

Substituting the given values $r_0 = 10 \times 10^{-14} \text{ m} = 10^{-13} \text{ m}$:

$K = \dfrac{(9 \times 10^9) \times (79 \times 2) \times (1.6 \times 10^{-19})^2}{10^{-13}}$

$K = \dfrac{9 \times 10^9 \times 158 \times 2.56 \times 10^{-38}}{10^{-13}}$

$K = 9 \times 158 \times 2.56 \times 10^{9 - 38 + 13}$

$K = 3640.32 \times 10^{-16} \text{ J}$

$K = 3.64032 \times 10^{-13} \text{ J}$

Rounding to the nearest value, we get $K = 3.64 \times 10^{-13} \text{ J}$.

Answer: $3.64 \times 10^{-13} \mathrm{ J}$

23338.subject: Physics
23338.text: A glass slab of 16 cm thickness has its bottom surface silvered. An air bubble is located inside the glass slab at a distance of 8 cm from the top surface. The refractive index of glass is 1.6. Which of the following correctly represents the number of images seen by an observer looking vertically downwards from air onto the top surface?
options: Only one image is seen at a depth of 5 cm
Multiple images are formed due to multiple reflections and refractions
Only one image is seen at a depth of 16 cm
Two images are seen at depths 5cm and 15 cm
23338.sol:
The observer will see two primary images of the air bubble.

The first image is formed by the direct refraction of light from the bubble through the top surface of the glass slab.
Real depth of the bubble from the top surface, $x_1 = 8$ cm.
Apparent depth of the first image, $d_1 = \dfrac{x_1}{\mu} = \dfrac{8}{1.6} = 5$ cm.

The second image is formed by the light that travels downwards, reflects from the silvered bottom surface, and then refracts out through the top surface.
Distance of the bubble from the bottom silvered surface = $16 - 8 = 8$ cm.
The silvered bottom acts as a plane mirror and forms an image of the bubble at a distance of $8$ cm behind it.
Total real depth of this reflected image from the top surface, $x_2 = 16 + 8 = 24$ cm.
Apparent depth of the second image, $d_2 = \dfrac{x_2}{\mu} = \dfrac{24}{1.6} = 15$ cm.

Thus, two images are seen at depths of $5$ cm and $15$ cm.

Answer: Two images are seen at depths 5cm and 15 cm

23521.subject: Physics
23521.text: The rate of heat conduction in the given two metal rods having the same length is found to be the same when the temperature difference between the ends is kept $30^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ If the area of cross section of the first rod is $8 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{ m}^2$ then what will be area of cross section of the second rod? [ Given that the ratio of the thermal conductivity of the first rod to that of the second rod is $1: 4$ ]
23521.sol:
The rate of heat conduction $H$ through a rod is given by the formula $H = \dfrac{KA \Delta T}{L}$, where $K$ is the thermal conductivity, $A$ is the area of cross-section, $\Delta T$ is the temperature difference, and $L$ is the length of the rod.

Given that the rate of heat conduction is the same for both rods, we have $H_1 = H_2$. Substituting the formula for both rods:

$\dfrac{K_1 A_1 \Delta T_1}{L_1} = \dfrac{K_2 A_2 \Delta T_2}{L_2}$

Since the lengths $L_1 = L_2$ and the temperature differences $\Delta T_1 = \Delta T_2 = 30^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ are the same, the equation simplifies to:

$K_1 A_1 = K_2 A_2$

Rearranging to solve for $A_2$:

$A_2 = A_1 \times \left( \dfrac{K_1}{K_2} \right)

Given $A_1 = 8 $\times10^{-2} \mathrm{ m}^2$ and the ratio $\dfrac{K_1}{K_2} = \dfrac{1}{4}$, we substitute these values:

$ A_2 = (8 \times10^{-2}) \times \left( \dfrac{1}{4} \right) =2 \times10^{-2} \mathrm{ m}^2$

Answer: $2 \times10^{-2} \mathrm{ m}^2$

23723.subject: Physics
23723.text: With what velocity should an observer approach a stationary sound source, so that the apparent frequency of sound should appear double the actual frequency?
23723.sol:
The apparent frequency $f'$ heard by an observer moving towards a stationary source is given by the Doppler effect formula:

$f' = f \left( \dfrac{v + v_o}{v} \right)

where $f$ is the actual frequency, $v$ is the speed of sound, and $v_o$ is the velocity of the observer.

Given that the apparent frequency is double the actual frequency, we have $f' = 2f$. Substituting this into the formula:

$2f = f $\left( \dfrac{v + v_o}{v} \right)$

Dividing both sides by $f$:

$2 = \dfrac{v + v_o}{v}$

$2v = v + v_o$

$v_o = v$

Answer: $v$

25889.text:
Let $\mathbb{R}^3$ denote the three-dimensional space. Take two points $P=(1,2,3)$ and $Q=(4,2,7)$. Let $\operatorname{dist}(X, Y)$ denote the distance between two points $X$ and $Y$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Let
$\begin{gathered}S=\left\{X \in \mathbb{R}^3:(\operatorname{dist}(X, P))^2-(\operatorname{dist}(X, Q))^2=50\right\} \text{ and } \\T=\left\{Y \in \mathbb{R}^3:(\operatorname{dist}(Y, Q))^2-(\operatorname{dist}(Y, P))^2=50\right\} .\end{gathered}$
Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE?
options: There is a triangle whose area is 1 and all of whose vertices are from $S$.
There are two distinct points $L$ and $M$ in $T$ such that each point on the line segment $L M$ is also in $T$.
There are infinitely many rectangles of perimeter 48 , two of whose vertices are from $S$ and the other two vertices are from $T$.
There is a square of perimeter 48 , two of whose vertices are from $S$ and the other two vertices are from $T$.
25889.sol: $\begin{aligned}& \mathrm{S}=\left\{\mathrm{X}:(\mathrm{XP})^2-(\mathrm{XQ})^2=50\right\} \\& \mathrm{T}=\left\{\mathrm{Y}:(\mathrm{YQ})^2-(\mathrm{YP})^2=50\right\}\end{aligned}$ for finding $S \equiv X(x, y, z)$ and for $T \equiv Y(x, y, z) \begin{aligned}&\left((x-1)^2+(y-1)^2+(\mathrm{z}-1)^2\right)-\left((\mathrm{x}-4)^2+(\mathrm{y}-2)^2+(\mathrm{z}-7)^2\right)=50 \\& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{S}=\{(\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y}, \mathrm{z}): 6 \mathrm{x}+8 \mathrm{z}=105\} \\& \mathrm{T}=\{(\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y}, \mathrm{z}): 6 \mathrm{x}+8 \mathrm{z}=5\}\end{aligned}$ Since $\mathrm{S}$ and $\mathrm{T}$ both are plane ; (1) There exist a triangle in plane $\mathrm{S}$ whose area $=1$ (always) (2) $\mathrm{L} ~\&~ \mathrm{M}$ lies on plane $\mathrm{T}$, hence line segment joining $\mathrm{L} \& \mathrm{M}$ will lie on plane $\mathrm{T}$. (3) Distance between $\mathrm{S} \& \mathrm{~T} \mathrm{d}=\left|\frac{105-5}{10}\right|=10$ Hence for rectangle of perimeter 48 can exist. (4) For Square There will be infinite such rectangle possible. Hence Answers 1,2,3,4 are correct.

28526.subject: Chemistry
28526.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
28526.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R:

Assertion A: The first ionisation enthalpy decreases across a period.

Reason R: The increasing nuclear charge outweighs the shielding across the period.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
28526.sol:
Ionization enthalpy is defined as the minimum amount of energy that is required to remove the most loosely bounded electron that is the electron present in the outermost shell, from an isolated gaseous atom.

First, ionisation energy increases along the period because effective nuclear charge increases. Along the period $Z$ increases which outweighs the shielding effect.

Hence, option C is the answer.

31428.subject: Chemistry
31428.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Gypsum is used for making fireproof wall boards.

Reason (R): Gypsum is unstable at high temperatures.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
31428.sol:
Gypsum board is also known as plasterboard, drywall or wall board. It consists of the paper surface and non-combustible core. These boards are easy to install. It has excellent fire resistance. Helps in sound isolation by preventing the transfer of unnecessary sound. It is less expensive and has great durability.

When exposed to high temperatures, gypsum only delays the temperature rise and cannot prevent shrinkage and crack from occurring, which can lead to the eventual collapse or failure of gypsum-based products.

Hence, both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

31633.subject: Chemistry
31633.text: When $0.25$ moles of a non-volatile, non-ionizable solute was dissolved in $1$ mole of a solvent the vapor pressure of solution was $x\%$ of vapor pressure of pure solvent. What is $x\%$?
31633.sol:
Moles of solute, $n_B = 0.25$

Moles of solvent, $n_A = 1$

Mole fraction of solvent, $X_A = \dfrac{n_A}{n_A + n_B} = \dfrac{1}{1 + 0.25} = \dfrac{1}{1.25} = 0.8$

According to Raoult's law, the vapor pressure of the solution is given by $P_s = P^0 X_A$

$P_s = 0.8 P^0 = 80\% \text{ of } P^0$

Thus, the vapor pressure of the solution is $80\%$ of the vapor pressure of the pure solvent.

Answer: $80\%$

31736.sol:
Raoult’s law states that a solvent’s partial vapour pressure in a solution (or mixture) is equal or identical to the vapour pressure of the pure solvent multiplied by its mole fraction in the solution.

Raoult’s law is valid only in the case of ideal solutions

${P}_{A} = {P}^{o}A{χ}_{A}\left(AccordingtoRaoult ' slaw\right)$

${P}_{A} = {P}_{T}{Y}_{A}\left(AccordingtoDalton ' slaw\right){P}_{T} = Totalpressure{P}_{A} = vapourpressureofAinsolution$

${P}^{o}A = VapourpressureofpureliquidA$

${χ}_{A} = MolefractionofcomponentAinliquidphase$

${Y}_{A} = MolefractionofcomponentAingaseousphase$

So, ${P}_{A} = {P}^{o}A{χ}_{A} = {Y}_{A}{P}_{T}$

${P}_{A}^{o}\left(0 . 2\right) = 0 . 5 \times 0 . 8$

${P}_{A}^{o} = 2atm$

33447.text: Let $m, n \in N$ and $gcd\left(2, n\right) = 1$. If $30\left(\begin{array}{ll}30 \\ 0\end{array}\right) + 29\left(\begin{array}{ll}30 \\ 1\end{array}\right) + \ldots . . + 2\left(\begin{array}{ll}30 \\ 28\end{array}\right) + 1\left(\begin{array}{ll}30 \\ 29\end{array}\right) = n . {2}^{m}$, then $n + m$ is equal to _______. (Here $\left(\begin{array}{ll}n \\ k\end{array}\right) = Ck n$)
33447.sol:
$30\left(C0 30\right) + 29\left(C1 30\right) + \ldots + 2\left(C28 30\right) + 1\left(C29 30\right)$

$= 30\left(C30 30\right) + 29\left(C29 30\right) + \ldots \ldots + 2\left(C2 30\right) + 1\left(C1 30\right)$

$= \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{30}r\left(Cr 30\right)$

$= \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{30}r\left(\dfrac{30}{r}\right)\left(Cr - 1 29\right)$

$= 30\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{30} Cr - 1 29$

$= 30\left(C0 29 + C1 29 + C2 29 + \ldots + C29 29\right)$

$= 30\left({2}^{29}\right) = 15{\left(2\right)}^{30} = n{\left(2\right)}^{m}$

Thus, for continuity of the given function, we have

$\lim_{x \to 0}f\left(x\right) = \alpha$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{{x}^{3}}{( 1 - cos2x{)}^{2}}{\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1 + 2x{e}^{- 2x}}{{\left(1 - x{e}^{- x}\right)}^{2}}\right)\right] = \alpha$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{{x}^{4}}{4x\sin^{4}x}\left(\dfrac{2x{e}^{- 2x} \cdot {\log}_{e}\left(1 + 2x{e}^{- 2x}\right)}{2x{e}^{- 2x}} + \dfrac{2x{e}^{- x} \cdot {\log}_{e}\left(1 - x{e}^{- x}\right)}{- x{e}^{- x}}\right)\right] = \alpha$

Now, using the standard limits $\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{sinx}{x}\right) = 1 \text{ and } \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{{\log}_{e}\left(1 + x\right)}{x}\right) = 1,$ we get

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{1}{4x}\left(2x{e}^{- 2x} + 2x{e}^{- x}\right)\right] = \alpha$$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{2x}{4x}\left({e}^{- 2x} + {e}^{- x}\right)\right] = \alpha$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{1}{2}\left({e}^{- 2x} + {e}^{- x}\right)\right] = \alpha$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}\left(2\right) = \alpha$

$⇒ \alpha = 1 .$

34720.text: Let $\alphax = exp\left({x}^{\beta}{y}^{\gamma}\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation $2{x}^{2}ydy - \left(1 - x{y}^{2}\right)dx = 0$, $x > 0, y\left(2\right) = \sqrt{{\log}_{e}2}$. Then $\alpha + \beta - \gamma$ equals :

$\alphax = {e}^{{x}^{\beta} \cdot {y}^{\gamma}} . . . . . . ( 1 )$

Now calculating the solution of differential equation,

$2{x}^{2}y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 - x{y}^{2}$

$∴ {x}^{2}\dfrac{dt}{dx} = 1 - xt$

$\dfrac{dt}{dx} + \dfrac{t}{x} = \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}} . . . . . ( 2 )$

Above differential equation is linear in $t$

We know solutions of differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q$ is given by,

$y . {e}^{∫ Pdx} = ∫ Q . {e}^{∫ Pdx} + C ( {e}^{∫ Pdx} = I . F . )$

Now calculating, $I . F . = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx} = {e}^{lnx} = x$

Therefore, the solution of equation $\left(2\right)$ is given by,

$t . x = ∫ \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}} \cdot xdx + C$

$⇒ {y}^{2} \cdot x = lnx + C$

$∵ y ( 2 ) = \sqrt{ln2}$

$∴ 2 . ln2 = ln2 + C ⇒ C = ln2$

Hence, solution is $x{y}^{2} = lnx + ln2$

$⇒ x{y}^{2} = ln2x$

$⇒ 2x = {e}^{x \cdot {y}^{2}} . . . . . . ( 3 )$

On comparing equations $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(3\right)$ we get,

$\alpha = 2, \beta = 1, \gamma = 2$

$∴ \alpha + \beta - \gamma = 1$

37439.subject: Mathematics
37439.text: Let $R$ be a relation defined on $\mathbb{N}$ as a $R$ b is $2a + 3b$ is a multiple of $5, a, b \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $R$ is
37439.sol:
Given:

$R = \left\{\left(a, b\right): 2a + 3bisdivisibleby5fora, b \in N\right\}$

Reflexive:

$2a + 3a = 5a$ is always divisible by $5$.

So, $\left(a, a\right) \in R$

Symmetric:

Let $\left(a, b\right) \in R$ i.e., $2a + 3b = 5\lambda$, where $\lambda \in {Z}^{+}$.

Now,

$5a + 5b = multipleof5$

$⇒ \left(2a + 3b\right) + \left(2b + 3a\right) = multipleof5$

$⇒ 5\lambda + \left(2b + 3a\right) = multipleof5$

$⇒ 2b + 3a = multipleof5 - 5\lambda$

So, $2b + 3a$ is divisible by $5$

Transitive:

Let $\left(a, b\right), \left(b, c\right) \in R$, then

$2a + 3b = 5{\lambda}_{1}; {\lambda}_{1} \in {Z}^{+}$

$2b + 3c = 5{\lambda}_{2}; {\lambda}_{2} \in {Z}^{+}$

So,

$2a + 5b + 3c = 5\left({\lambda}_{1} + {\lambda}_{2}\right)$

$⇒ 2a + 3c = 5\left({\lambda}_{1} + {\lambda}_{2} - b\right)$

Hence, $2a + 3c$ is divisible by $5$, so $\left(a, c\right) \in R$

Hence, $R$ is an equivalence relation.

37758.text: Let Abe the $set of all points \left(\alpha, \beta\right) such that the area of triangle formed by the points \left(5, 6\right)$, $\left(3, 2\right)$ and $\left(\alpha, \beta\right)$ is $12$ square units. 37758.sol:

$∴ \dfrac{1}{2}\left|\begin{cases}\alpha & \beta & 1 \\ 5 & 6 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 12$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}\alpha & \beta & 1 \\ 5 & 6 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 24$

$⇒ \alpha\left(6 - 2\right) - \beta\left(5 - 3\right) + 1\left(10 - 18\right) = \pm 24$

$⇒ 4\alpha - 2\beta - 8 = \pm 24$

$⇒ 4\alpha - 2\beta = 32, 4\alpha - 2\beta + 16 = 0$

$⇒ 2\alpha - \beta - 16 = 0, 2\alpha - \beta + 8 = 0$

So point will be either $\left(\alpha, 2\alpha + 8\right), \left(\alpha, 2\alpha - 16\right)$

For the point $\left(\alpha, 2\alpha + 8\right)$,

Distance from origin
$D = \sqrt{{\alpha}^{2} + ( 2\alpha + 8{)}^{2}} = \sqrt{5{\alpha}^{2} + 32\alpha + 64}\left(∵ \beta = 2\alpha + 8\right)$

$⇒ {D}^{2} = 5{\alpha}^{2} + 32\alpha + 64$

For maximum or minimum length,

$\dfrac{d\left({D}^{2}\right)}{d\alpha} = 10\alpha + 32 = 0$

$⇒ \alpha = - \dfrac{16}{5}$

$∴ \beta = \dfrac{- 32}{5} + 8 = \dfrac{8}{5}$

$∴ D = \sqrt{{\left(- \dfrac{16}{5}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{8}{5}\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{8}{5}\sqrt{5} = \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{5}}$

Similarly if $\beta = 2\alpha - 16, D = \sqrt{{\alpha}^{2} + {\left(2\alpha - 16\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{5{\alpha}^{2} - 64\alpha + 256}$

$∴ {D}^{2} = 5{\alpha}^{2} - 64\alpha + 256$

For maximum or minimum length,

$\dfrac{d\left({D}^{2}\right)}{d\alpha} = 0$

$⇒ 10\alpha - 64 = 0$

$∴ \alpha = \dfrac{32}{5}$

$∴ D = \sqrt{{\left(\dfrac{32}{5}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{64}{5} - 16\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{16}{\sqrt{5}}$at $\alpha = \dfrac{32}{5}$
So, least possible length of line segment is $\dfrac{8}{\sqrt{5}}$

Expanding $|\vec{a} - \vec{b}|^2 + |\vec{b} - \vec{c}|^2 + |\vec{c} - \vec{a}|^2 = 9$ with unit vectors gives $6 - 2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}) = 9$.

For the symmetric case where vectors are equally spaced (e.g., on a circle at 120° intervals), we have $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} = \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a} = -1/2$.
Expanding $|2\vec{a} + k\vec{b} + k\vec{c}|^2 = 9$ gives $4 + 2k^2 + 4k(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}) + 2k^2\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} = 9$.
Substituting the symmetric values: $4 + 2k^2(1/2) + 4k(-1) + 2k^2(-1/2) = 9$, which simplifies to $k^2 - 4k - 5 = 0$.
Factoring: $(k-5)(k+1) = 0$, giving $k = 5$ as the positive solution.

38567.text: Let $\overset{^}{a}$ and $\overset{^}{b}$ be two unit vectors such that the angle between them is $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$. If $\theta$ is the angle between the vectors $\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right)$ and $\left(\overset{^}{a} + 2\overset{^}{b} + 2\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right)$ then the value of $164\cos^{2}\theta$ is equal to
38567.sol:
Let $\overset{^}{a}$ and $\overset{^}{b}$ be two unit vectors such that the angle between them is $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$. If $\theta$ is the angle between the vectors $\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right)$ and $\left(\overset{^}{a} + 2\overset{^}{b} + 2\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right)$ then the value of $164\cos^{2}\theta$ is equal to

Now let angle between $\overset{^}{a} \text{ and } \overset{^}{b} = \dfrac{\pi}{4} = ϕ$

So, $\overset{^}{a} \cdot \overset{^}{b} = \left|\overset{^}{a}\right|\left|\overset{^}{b}\right|cosϕ$

$⇒ \overset{^}{a} \cdot \overset{^}{b} = cosϕ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Now finding angle between $\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right) \text{ and } \left(\overset{^}{a} + 2\overset{^}{b} + 2\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right)$ we get,

$cos\theta = \dfrac{\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{^}{a} + 2\overset{^}{b} + 2\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right)}{\left|\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right|\left|\overset{^}{a} + 2\overset{^}{b} + 2\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right|} . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now finding the value of ${\left|\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right|}^{2} = \left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right)$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right|}^{2} = 2 + 2\overset{^}{a} \cdot \overset{^}{b}$$= 2 + \sqrt{2}$

Also value of $\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b} = \left|\overset{^}{a}\right|\left|\overset{^}{b}\right|sinϕ\overset{^}{n}$

$⇒ \overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b} = \overset{^}{n}\sqrt{2}$ when $\overset{^}{n}$ is vector $⊥$to $\overset{^}{a}$ and $\overset{^}{b}$

Let $\overset{\to}{c} = \overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}$

We know that, $\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = 0$ and $\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 0$ as perpendicular vector dot product is zero.

Now value of ${\left|\overset{^}{a} + 2\overset{^}{b} + 2\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2}$

$= 1 + 4 + \dfrac{\left(4\right)}{2} + 4\overset{^}{a} \cdot \overset{^}{b} + 8\overset{^}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} + 4\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{^}{a}$

$= 7 + \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{2}} = 7 + 2\sqrt{2}$

Now finding dot product we get, $\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{^}{a} + 2\overset{^}{b} + 2\overset{\to}{c}\right)$

$= {\left|\overset{^}{a}\right|}^{2} + 2\overset{^}{a} \cdot \overset{^}{b} + 0 + \overset{^}{b} \cdot \overset{^}{a} + 2{\left|\overset{^}{b}\right|}^{2} + 0$

$= 1 + \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + 2$

$= 3 + \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{2}}$

Now putting all the values in equation $\left(1\right)$ we get,

$cos\theta = \dfrac{3 + \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{2}}}{\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2}}\sqrt{7 + 2\sqrt{2}}}$

$⇒ \cos^{2}\theta = \dfrac{9{\left(\sqrt{2} + 1\right)}^{2}}{2\left(2 + \sqrt{2}\right)\left(7 + 2\sqrt{2}\right)}$

$⇒ \cos^{2}\theta = \left(\dfrac{9}{2\sqrt{2}}\right)\dfrac{\left(\sqrt{2} + 1\right)}{\left(7 + 2\sqrt{2}\right)}$

$⇒ 164\cos^{2}\theta = \dfrac{\left(82\right)\left(9\right)}{\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{\left(\sqrt{2} + 1\right)}{\left(7 + 2\sqrt{2}\right)}\dfrac{\left(7 - 2\sqrt{2}\right)}{\left(7 - 2\sqrt{2}\right)}$

$⇒ 164\cos^{2}\theta = \dfrac{\left(82\right)}{\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{\left(9\right)\left[7\sqrt{2} - 4 + 7 - 2\sqrt{2}\right]}{\left(41\right)}$

$⇒ 164\cos^{2}\theta = \left(9\sqrt{2}\right)\left[5\sqrt{2} + 3\right]$

$⇒ 164\cos^{2}\theta = 90 + 27\sqrt{2}$

39154.text: Two identical thin metal plates has charge ${q}_{1}$ and ${q}_{2}$ respectively such that ${q}_{1} > {q}_{2}$. The plates were brought close to each other to form a parallel plate capacitor of capacitance $C$. The potential difference between them is :
39154.sol:
On bringing the charged metal plates closer, electric field $\overset{\to}{E}$ in the intervening space is $\overset{\to}{E} = \overset{\to}{{E}_{1}} + \overset{\to}{{E}_{2}}$

Where

Intensity of field due plate charged by ${q}_{1}$ is $\left|\overset{\to}{{E}_{1}}\right| = \dfrac{{\sigma}_{1}}{2{ε}_{0}} = \dfrac{{q}_{1}}{2{ε}_{0}A}$(directed rightwards)

And Intensity of field due to plate charged by ${q}_{2}$ is

$\left|\overset{\to}{{E}_{2}}\right| = \dfrac{{\sigma}_{2}}{2{ε}_{0}} = \dfrac{{q}_{2}}{2{ε}_{0}A}$ (directed leftwards)
So, Net field is given by

$\overset{\to}{E} = \overset{\to}{{E}_{1}} + \overset{\to}{{E}_{2}} ⇒ E = {E}_{1} - {E}_{2}$

$∴ E = \dfrac{{q}_{1}}{2{ε}_{0}A} - \dfrac{{q}_{2}}{2{ε}_{0}A} = \dfrac{\left({q}_{1} - {q}_{2}\right)}{2{ε}_{0}A} . . . \left(1\right)$

For parallel plate capacitor $C = \dfrac{{ε}_{0}A}{d} . . . \left(2\right)$

From above two equations

$E = \dfrac{\left({q}_{1} - {q}_{2}\right)}{2C}d . . . \left(3\right)$

$∵$Relation between intensity of field $\left(E\right)$ and potential difference $\left(V\right)$ between the plates is

$E = \dfrac{V}{d} . . . \left(4\right)$

From equation $\left(3\right)$ and $\left(4\right)$

$V = \dfrac{\left({q}_{1} - {q}_{2}\right)}{2C}$

39401.text:
The amplitude of $15sin ( 1000\pit )$ is modulated by $10sin ( 4\pit )$ signal. The amplitude modulated signal contains frequencies of

A. $500Hz$

B. $2Hz$

C. $250Hz$

D. $498Hz$

E. $502Hz$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
39401.sol:
The carrier wave frequency is given by

$\begin{cases}{f}_{c} & = & \dfrac{1000\pi}{2\pi} \\ & = & 500Hz\end{cases}$

The modulating wave frequency is given by

$\begin{cases}{f}_{m} & = & \dfrac{4\pi}{2\pi} \\ & = & 2Hz\end{cases}$

Hence, the frequencies contained in the modulated signal are given by

$\begin{cases}f & = & {f}_{c} - {f}_{m}, {f}_{m}, {f}_{c} + {f}_{m} \\ = & 498Hz, 500Hz, 502Hz\end{cases}$

40398.text: A plane polarized monochromatic EM wave is travelling a vacuum along $z$ direction such that at $\mathrm{t}=\mathrm{t}_1$ it is found that the electric field is zero at a spatial point $z_1$. Using $E=E_0-e^i(k z-\omega t)$
Given, at $t=t_1, z=z_1, E=0$
the next zero that occurs in it's neighborhood is at $z_2$, the frequency of the electromagnetic wave at $t_2\begin{aligned}$&e^{i$\left($k z_1-$\omega$t_1\right)}=e^{i$\left($k z_2-$\omega$t_2\right)} \\
&k z_1-$\omega$t_1=k z_2-$\omega$t_2 \\
&$\left($t_2-t_1\right) $\omega=$k$\left($z-z_1\right) \\
&$\text{ where }$k=$\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}=$2 $\pi$v \\
&$\left($t_2-t_1\right)=$\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda \times 2 \pi v}\left($z_2-z_1\right)
\end{aligned}

$\begin{aligned}$&\quad=$\frac{1}{x \times v}\left($z_2-z_1\right) \\
&\Rightarrow \lambda $\times$v=$\frac{\left(z_2-z_1\right)}{\left(t_2-t_1\right)}=$C \\
&\quad$\left($t_2-t_1\right)=$\frac{\left(z_2-z_1\right)}{C}$\\
&$\text{ Frequency is }$f \propto $\frac{1}{t} \text{ then } \frac{1}{\left(t_2-t_1\right)}=\frac{C}{\left(z_2-z_1\right)}$\\
&\therefore $\text{ Frequency, }$f=$\frac{3 \times 10^8}{\left(z_2-z_1\right)}
\end{aligned}$

The temperature of $3 . 00mol$ of an ideal diatomic gas is increased by $40 . 0 ° C$ without changing the pressure of the gas. The molecules in the gas rotate but do not oscillate. $
41542.sol:

41880.subject: Physics
41880.text: A cylindrical vessel of $40$ cm radius is completely filled with water and its capacity is $528$ dm$^3$ (dm : decimeter). The vessel is placed on a solid block of exactly same height as vessel. If a small hole is made at $70$ cm below the top of water level, then horizontal range of water falling on the ground in the beginning is __________ cm.
41880.sol:
Volume of the cylindrical vessel, $V = 528$ dm$^3 = 528000$ cm$^3$

Radius of the vessel, $r = 40$ cm

Let the height of the vessel be $H$.

$V = \pi r^2 H$

$528000 = \dfrac{22}{7} \times (40)^2 \times H$

$H = \dfrac{528000 \times 7}{22 \times 1600} = 105$ cm

The vessel is placed on a block of height equal to the vessel, so the height of the block is $105$ cm.

Depth of the hole from the top water level, $h = 70$ cm

Height of the hole from the ground, $y = \text{Height of block} + (H - h)$

$y = 105 + (105 - 70) = 140$ cm

Velocity of efflux, $v = \sqrt{2gh}$

Time of flight of water, $t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2y}{g}}$

Horizontal range, $R = v \times t = \sqrt{2gh} \times \sqrt{\dfrac{2y}{g}} = 2\sqrt{hy}$

$R = 2\sqrt{70 \times 140} = 2\sqrt{70 \times 70 \times 2} = 140\sqrt{2}$ cm

Answer: $140\sqrt{2}$

$x\left(t\right) = rcos\left(\theta + \phi\right) . . . \left(2\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (2) to obtain the required expression

$x ( t ) = rcos\left(\omegat + \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$

47733.subject: Chemistry
47733.text: The highest oxidation state of manganese in fluoride is $+4$ ($\text{MnF}_4$), but the highest oxidation state in oxides is $+7$ ($\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7$), because
options: Fluorine is more electronegative than oxygen
In covalent compounds, fluorine can form single bond only, while oxygen forms double bond
47733.sol:
The ability of oxygen to stabilize the highest oxidation states of transition metals (such as $+7$ for $\text{Mn}$ in $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7$) is due to its ability to form multiple bonds (double bonds) with the metal atoms.

Fluorine can only form single bonds. To achieve a $+7$ oxidation state with fluorine, a single manganese atom would have to accommodate seven fluorine atoms around it, which is sterically highly unfavorable and thus $\text{MnF}_7$ does not exist.

In $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7$, manganese forms double bonds with oxygen atoms, requiring fewer ligands around the central metal atom and thereby reducing steric hindrance.

Answer: In covalent compounds, fluorine can form single bond only, while oxygen forms double bond

55128.subject: Chemistry
55128.text: Identify the reagent used in the transformation of Ketone into semicarbazone.
55128.sol:
The transformation of a ketone into a semicarbazone involves the reaction of the ketone with semicarbazide.

The chemical formula of semicarbazide is $\text{NH}_2-\text{NH}-\text{CONH}_2$.

The reaction proceeds via nucleophilic addition followed by the elimination of a water molecule, resulting in the formation of a semicarbazone ($ > \text{C}=\text{N}-\text{NH}-\text{CONH}_2$).

Other reagents given:
$\text{NH}_2-\text{OH}$ (hydroxylamine) forms an oxime.
$\text{NH}_2-\text{NH}_2$ (hydrazine) forms a hydrazone.
$\text{NH}_2-\text{NH}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$ (phenylhydrazine) forms a phenylhydrazone.

Answer: $\text{NH}_2-\text{NH}-\text{CONH}_2$

55791.subject: Chemistry
55791.text: What different types of bonds are formed by chlorine with oxygen in perchloric acid?
55791.sol:
Perchloric acid structure: Chlorine acts as the central atom bonded to four oxygen atoms, with one oxygen also bonded to hydrogen.

Total valence electrons: H (1) + Cl (7) + 4×O (24) = 32.

Initial bonding uses 5 bonds (Cl-O and O-H), consuming 10 electrons.
Remaining 22 electrons distribute as lone pairs: terminal O-H oxygen receives 2 pairs, three Cl-O oxygens each receive 3 pairs.

Formal charges reveal instability: Cl (+3), three oxygens (-1) each. Minimizing charges by converting lone pairs to bonds yields the optimal structure.

Final configuration shows chlorine bonded via:
• One single bond to oxygen in O-H group
• Three double bonds to remaining oxygen atoms

$\text{FC}_{\text{Cl}} = 7 - 0 - \frac{1}{2}(2 + 3\times4) = 0$
$\text{FC}_{\text{O}} = 6 - 4 - \frac{1}{2}(4) = 0$ for double-bonded oxygens

Thus chlorine forms one single bond and three double bonds with oxygen.

58382.sol:
To determine which polymer is obtained by condensation polymerisation, let us analyze each option:

1. $[\,\text{CF}_2 - \text{CF}_2\,]_n$ is Teflon (Polytetrafluoroethylene). It is formed by the addition polymerisation of tetrafluoroethene.

2. $[\,\text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}_2\,]_n$ is Polythene. It is formed by the addition polymerisation of ethene.

3. $[\,\text{NH} - (\text{CH}_2)_5 - \text{CO}\,]_n$ is Nylon 6. It is synthesized by the ring-opening polymerisation of caprolactam. Since no small molecule is eliminated during the process, it is technically considered an addition polymerisation.

4. The polymer shown in the image is Nylon 6,6, which has the repeating unit $[\,-\text{CO}-(\text{CH}_2)_4-\text{CO}-\text{NH}-(\text{CH}_2)_6-\text{NH}-\,]_n$. It is formed by the condensation polymerisation of adipic acid and hexamethylenediamine, accompanied by the elimination of water molecules.

Therefore, Nylon 6,6 is the polymer obtained by the condensation polymerisation method.

58609.subject: Chemistry
58609.text: What is the oxidation number of carbon in oxalic acid ?
58609.sol:
The chemical formula of oxalic acid is $H_2C_2O_4$.

Let the oxidation number of carbon be $x$.

The oxidation number of hydrogen is $+1$ and that of oxygen is $-2$.

The sum of oxidation numbers of all atoms in a neutral molecule is zero.

$2(+1) + 2(x) + 4(-2) = 0$

$2 + 2x - 8 = 0$

$2x - 6 = 0$

$2x = 6$

$x = +3$

The oxidation number of carbon in oxalic acid is $+3$.

Answer: $+3$

59171.subject: Chemistry
59171.text: $Calculate the concentration of an aqueous solution of non electrolyte at 300 K if its osmotic pressure is 12 atm.  \left[\mathrm{R}=0.0821 \mathrm{ atm} \mathrm{dm}^3 \mathrm{ K}^{-1} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}\right]$
59171.sol:
The concentration is determined using the Van't Hoff equation for osmotic pressure: $\Pi = CRT$, where $\Pi = 12\text{ atm}$, $T = 300\text{ K}$, and $R = 0.0821\text{ atm dm}^3\text{ K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$.

Rearranging gives $C = \frac{\Pi}{RT} = \frac{12}{0.0821 \times 300}$.

Calculating the denominator: $0.0821 \times 300 = 24.63$, so $C = \frac{12}{24.63} \approx 0.4872\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.

This corresponds to $0.487\text{ M}$, matching option B.

60719.text: The equation of the circle concentric with circle $x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 7 = 0$ and which touches the line $x + y + 3 = 0$ is....
60719.sol:
The given circle is $x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 7 = 0$.

Its center is $(3,0)$.

The required circle is concentric with the given circle, so its center is also $(3,0)$.

The required circle touches the line $x + y + 3 = 0$.

The radius $r$ of the required circle is the perpendicular distance from the center $(3,0)$ to the line $x + y + 3 = 0$.

$r = \dfrac{|3 + 0 + 3|}{\sqrt{1^2 + 1^2}} = \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{2}} = 3\sqrt{2}$

The equation of the required circle is $(x - 3)^2 + (y - 0)^2 = r^2$.

$(x - 3)^2 + y^2 = (3\sqrt{2})^2$

$x^2 - 6x + 9 + y^2 = 18$

$x^2 + y^2 - 6x - 9 = 0$

Answer: $x^2 + y^2 - 6x - 9 = 0$

61281.subject: Mathematics
61281.text: The equation of the curve passing through the point (0, 1) and having a slope of the tangent at point $P(x, y)$ is equal to $\dfrac{y}{x + y}$, is
61281.sol:
Given the slope of the tangent is $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x + y}$

Taking the reciprocal, we get:

$\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{x + y}{y}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{dx}{dy} - \dfrac{x}{y} = 1$

This is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dx}{dy} + Px = Q$, where $P = -\dfrac{1}{y}$ and $Q = 1$.

Integrating Factor (IF) $= e^{\int -\dfrac{1}{y} dy} = e^{-\ln y} = \dfrac{1}{y}$

The solution is given by:

$x \cdot (\text{IF}) = \int Q \cdot (\text{IF}) dy + C$

$\Rightarrow x \left(\dfrac{1}{y}\right) = \int \dfrac{1}{y} dy + C$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{x}{y} = \ln y + C$

Since the curve passes through the point $(0, 1)$, substitute $x = 0$ and $y = 1$:

$\dfrac{0}{1} = \ln 1 + C \Rightarrow C = 0$

Therefore, the equation of the curve is:

$\dfrac{x}{y} = \ln y$

$\Rightarrow y = e^{\dfrac{x}{y}}$

Answer: $y = e^{\frac{x}{y}}$

62173.sol:
The given integral is $I = \int \dfrac{x^4 + 1}{x^6 + 1} dx$

The denominator can be factored as $x^6 + 1 = (x^2)^3 + 1 = (x^2 + 1)(x^4 - x^2 + 1)$

Rewriting the numerator as $x^4 + 1 = (x^4 - x^2 + 1) + x^2$

$I = \int \dfrac{(x^4 - x^2 + 1) + x^2}{(x^2 + 1)(x^4 - x^2 + 1)} dx$

Separating the terms:

$I = \int \dfrac{x^4 - x^2 + 1}{(x^2 + 1)(x^4 - x^2 + 1)} dx + \int \dfrac{x^2}{x^6 + 1} dx$

$I = \int \dfrac{1}{x^2 + 1} dx + \dfrac{1}{3} \int \dfrac{3x^2}{(x^3)^2 + 1} dx$

Substituting $t = x^3 \Rightarrow dt = 3x^2 dx$ in the second integral:

$I = \tan^{-1}x + \dfrac{1}{3} \int \dfrac{1}{t^2 + 1} dt$

$I = \tan^{-1}x + \dfrac{1}{3} \tan^{-1}(t) + c$

$I = \tan^{-1}x + \dfrac{1}{3} \tan^{-1}(x^3) + c$

Answer: $\tan^{-1}x + \dfrac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}(x^3) + c$

62739.text: If $\mathrm{f}(x)=\frac{(27-2 x)^{\frac{1}{3}}-3}{9-3(243+5 x)^{\frac{1}{5}}}, x \neq 0$ is continuous at $x=0$, then the value of $f(0)$ is
62739.sol:
To ensure continuity at $x=0$, define $f(0) = \lim_{x \to 0} f(x)$ where

$f(x)=\frac{(27-2 x)^{\frac{1}{3}}-3}{9-3(243+5 x)^{\frac{1}{5}}}$.

Direct substitution yields the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}$, requiring further analysis.

Applying L'Hôpital's rule, differentiate numerator and denominator:

$N'(x) = -\frac{2}{3}(27-2x)^{-\frac{2}{3}}$

$D'(x) = -3(243+5x)^{-\frac{4}{5}}$

The limit becomes

$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{N'(x)}{D'(x)} = \frac{-\frac{2}{3}(27)^{-\frac{2}{3}}}{-3(243)^{-\frac{4}{5}}}$.

Expressing $27=3^3$ and $243=3^5$, we simplify:

$\frac{-\frac{2}{3} \cdot 3^{-2}}{-3 \cdot 3^{-4}} = \frac{-\frac{2}{27}}{-\frac{1}{27}} = 2$.

Alternatively, using the standard limit $\lim_{y \to 0} \frac{(a+y)^n - a^n}{y} = n a^{n-1}$, we compute numerator and denominator limits separately.

The numerator limit transforms to $-2 \cdot \frac{1}{3}(27)^{-\frac{2}{3}} = -\frac{2}{27}$.

The denominator limit becomes $-15 \cdot \frac{1}{5}(243)^{-\frac{4}{5}} = -\frac{1}{27}$.

The ratio confirms $\lim_{x \to 0} f(x) = 2$.

Final answer: $f(0) = 2$

62823.text: The difference between the maximum value and minimum value of the objective function $z = 3x + 5y$ of a linear programming problem subject to constraints $5x + 10y \leq 50$, $x + y \geq 1$, $y \leq 4$ and $x \geq 0, y \geq 0$ is $3\lambda$. Then the value of $\lambda$ is
62823.sol:
The given constraints are:
$5x + 10y \leq 50 \Rightarrow x + 2y \leq 10$
$x + y \geq 1$
$y \leq 4$
$x \geq 0, y \geq 0$

The feasible region is bounded by the lines $x + 2y = 10$, $x + y = 1$, $y = 4$, $x = 0$, and $y = 0$. Let us find the corner points of this feasible region:
Intersection of $x = 0$ and $x + y = 1 \Rightarrow (0,1)$
Intersection of $x = 0$ and $y = 4 \Rightarrow (0,4)$
Intersection of $y = 4$ and $x + 2y = 10 \Rightarrow x + 8 = 10 \Rightarrow x = 2 \Rightarrow (2,4)$
Intersection of $y = 0$ and $x + 2y = 10 \Rightarrow x = 10 \Rightarrow (10,0)$
Intersection of $y = 0$ and $x + y = 1 \Rightarrow x = 1 \Rightarrow (1,0)$

Now, we evaluate the objective function $z = 3x + 5y$ at each of these corner points:
At $(0,1)$, $z = 3(0) + 5(1) = 5$
At $(0,4)$, $z = 3(0) + 5(4) = 20$
At $(2,4)$, $z = 3(2) + 5(4) = 26$
At $(10,0)$, $z = 3(10) + 5(0) = 30$
At $(1,0)$, $z = 3(1) + 5(0) = 3$

From the above values, the maximum value of $z$ is $30$ and the minimum value of $z$ is $3$.

The difference between the maximum and minimum values is:
$30 - 3 = 27$

Given that this difference is equal to $3\lambda$, we have:
$3\lambda = 27 \Rightarrow \lambda = 9$

Answer: $9$.

62830.text: A manufacturing company produces two items, A and B. Each toy should be processed by two machines, I and II. Machine I can be operated for maximum 10 hours 40 minutes. It takes 20 minutes for an item A and 15 minutes for B. Machine II can be operated for a total time at 8 hours 20 minutes. It takes 5 minutes for an item $A$ and 8 minutes for $B$. The profit per item of $A$ is $₹ 25$ and per item of $B$ is ₹18. The formulation of an L.P.P. to maximize the profit (where $x$ is number of items $A$ and $y$ is the number of item $B$ ) is _____

Machine II operates for 500 minutes (8 hours 20 minutes), with processing times of 5 minutes per unit of A and 8 minutes per unit of B, giving $5x + 8y \leqslant 500$.

Non-negativity constraints require $x \geqslant 0$ and $y \geqslant 0$.

The complete formulation matches Option B:
Maximize $Z = 25x + 18y$
Subject to:
$20x + 15y \leqslant 640$
$5x + 8y \leqslant 500$
$x, y \geqslant 0$

64485.text: The equation of the plane passing through the line of intersection of the planes $x+y+z=1$ and $3 x+4 y+5 z=2$ and perpendicular to the XY- plane is
64485.sol:
A plane passing through the line of intersection of $x+y+z-1=0$ and $3x+4y+5z-2=0$ has the form $(x+y+z-1) + \lambda(3x+4y+5z-2) = 0$.

Simplifying gives $(1+3\lambda)x + (1+4\lambda)y + (1+5\lambda)z - (1+2\lambda) = 0$ with normal vector $\vec{n} = (1+3\lambda)\hat{i} + (1+4\lambda)\hat{j} + (1+5\lambda)\hat{k}$.

Since this plane is perpendicular to the XY-plane $z=0$ with normal $\hat{k}$, their dot product must vanish: $\vec{n} \cdot \hat{k} = 1+5\lambda = 0$.

Solving yields $\lambda = -\frac{1}{5}$.

Substituting gives $\frac{2}{5}x + \frac{1}{5}y - \frac{3}{5} = 0$, which after multiplying by 5 becomes $2x + y - 3 = 0$.

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{A}}$.

65084.text:
Let $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ be three vectors of equal magnitude such that the angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ is $\alpha$, $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$ is $\beta$, $\bar{c}$ and $\bar{a}$ is $\gamma$.
Then the minimum value of $\cos\alpha + \cos\beta + \cos\gamma$ is...
65084.sol:
Let the magnitude of the three vectors be $|\vec{a}| = |\vec{b}| = |\vec{c}| = x$.

The square of the magnitude of the sum of the three vectors is given by:

$|\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}|^2 = |\vec{a}|^2 + |\vec{b}|^2 + |\vec{c}|^2 + 2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a})$

Since the square of the magnitude of any vector is always non-negative:

$|\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}|^2 \ge 0$

$|\vec{a}|^2 + |\vec{b}|^2 + |\vec{c}|^2 + 2(|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|\cos\alpha + |\vec{b}||\vec{c}|\cos\beta + |\vec{c}||\vec{a}|\cos\gamma) \ge 0$

Substituting the magnitudes:

$x^2 + x^2 + x^2 + 2(x^2\cos\alpha + x^2\cos\beta + x^2\cos\gamma) \ge 0$

$3x^2 + 2x^2(\cos\alpha + \cos\beta + \cos\gamma) \ge 0$

Since $x^2 > 0$ (assuming non-zero vectors), dividing the entire inequality by $x^2$ gives:

$3 + 2(\cos\alpha + \cos\beta + \cos\gamma) \ge 0$

$2(\cos\alpha + \cos\beta + \cos\gamma) \ge -3$

$\cos\alpha + \cos\beta + \cos\gamma \ge -\dfrac{3}{2}$

Therefore, the minimum value of $\cos\alpha + \cos\beta + \cos\gamma$ is $-\dfrac{3}{2}$.

66303.text: By connecting a resistance of $980\ \Omega$ in series with a galvanometer, it is converted into a voltmeter of a certain range. When the resistance of $470\ \Omega$ is connected in series, the range is halved. The resistance of the galvanometer is
66303.sol:
Let the resistance of the galvanometer be $G$ and its full-scale deflection current be $I_g$.

When a resistance of $980\ \Omega$ is connected in series, the range of the voltmeter is $V$.

$V = I_g(G + 980)$

When a resistance of $470\ \Omega$ is connected in series, the range is halved to $\dfrac{V}{2}$.

$\dfrac{V}{2} = I_g(G + 470)$

Dividing the first equation by the second equation:

$2 = \dfrac{G + 980}{G + 470}$

$2G + 940 = G + 980$

$G = 40\ \Omega$

Answer: $40\ \Omega$

68667.text: The time taken by simple pendulum for one oscillation is T on earth's surface. Its time period becomes xT when taken to a height R (equal to earth's radius) above the earth's surface. The value of x is
68667.sol:
The time period of a simple pendulum on the surface of the earth is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}}$.

The acceleration due to gravity at a height $h$ above the earth's surface is $g' = \dfrac{g}{\left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right)^2}$.

Given $h = R$, we have $g' = \dfrac{g}{\left(1 + \dfrac{R}{R}\right)^2} = \dfrac{g}{4}$.

The new time period $T'$ at height $R$ is $T' = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g'}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{\dfrac{g}{4}}} = 2 \times 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}} = 2T$.

Since $T' = xT$, we get $x = 2$.

Answer: $2$

70958.subject: Biology
70958.text: Which of following group includes reducing sugars?
70958.sol:
Reducing sugars are carbohydrates that contain a free aldehyde or ketone group and can reduce Fehling's solution and Tollens' reagent.

All monosaccharides, such as glucose, fructose, and galactose, are reducing sugars.

Disaccharides in which the anomeric carbon of at least one monosaccharide unit is free are also reducing sugars. Examples include maltose and lactose.

In sucrose, the glycosidic bond is formed between the anomeric carbon of glucose (C1) and the anomeric carbon of fructose (C2). Since both anomeric carbons are involved in the linkage, there is no free hemiacetal or hemiketal group, making sucrose a non-reducing sugar.

Therefore, the group containing only reducing sugars is Glucose, Lactose, and Maltose.

Answer: Glucose, Lactose, Maltose

71005.text:
Match the Column- I with Column- II.
Column- I (Disorder)Column- II (Symptoms)
A) EmphysemaI) Difficulty in breathing, constriction of bronchioles
B) LaryngitisII) Breakdown of alveoli and shortness of breath.
C) PneumoniaIII) Inflammation of vocal cords and hoarseness of voice.

Emphysema is a chronic disorder in which alveolar walls are damaged, leading to a decrease in the respiratory surface area. This causes a breakdown of alveoli and shortness of breath. Thus, A matches with II.

Laryngitis is the inflammation of the larynx or vocal cords, which leads to hoarseness or loss of voice. Thus, B matches with III.

Pneumonia is an infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs, causing mild to severe inflammation, fever, and chest pain. Thus, C matches with IV.

Asthma is a respiratory condition marked by spasms in the bronchi of the lungs, causing difficulty in breathing and constriction of bronchioles. Thus, D matches with I.

The correct matching is A - II, B - III, C - IV, D - I.

Answer: A - II, B - III, C - IV, D - I

71148.text: The ________ are also called as cytotoxic T-cell.
71148.sol:
Cytotoxic T-cells are a type of T lymphocyte that directly kills infected or damaged cells, such as those infected by viruses or cancer cells.

Due to their direct killing mechanism, they are also known as killer T cells.

Suppressor T cells (regulatory T cells) suppress the immune response.

Memory T cells remember specific antigens for a faster response upon re-exposure.

Helper T cells assist other white blood cells in immunologic processes.

71469.subject: Biology
71469.text: Which one of the following respiratory reactions does NOT yield $\text{CO}_2$?
71469.sol:
In the conversion of pyruvic acid to acetyl CoA (link reaction), oxidative decarboxylation takes place, releasing $\text{CO}_2$.

In alcoholic fermentation, pyruvic acid is first converted to acetaldehyde, releasing $\text{CO}_2$, which is then reduced to ethanol. Thus, the overall conversion of pyruvic acid to ethanol also yields $\text{CO}_2$.

In lactic acid fermentation, pyruvic acid (a 3-carbon compound) is directly reduced to lactic acid (also a 3-carbon compound) by the enzyme lactate dehydrogenase. Since there is no loss of carbon atoms, no decarboxylation occurs and no $\text{CO}_2$ is produced.

Answer: Pyruvic acid → Lactic acid

71540.text: Alveolar wall is made up of ------- epithelium resting on a basement membrane of connective tissue.
71540.sol:
The alveolar wall is the primary site for the exchange of gases in the lungs.

For efficient diffusion of oxygen and carbon dioxide, the diffusion boundary must be extremely thin.

Therefore, the alveolar wall is composed of a single layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries, which is known as simple squamous epithelium.

This squamous epithelium rests on a thin basement membrane of connective tissue.

71550.subject: Biology
71550.text: Which of the following sets of conditions favour the opening of stomata?
options: Conversion of sugar to startch in guard cells, Formation of Potassium malate in the guard cells, Exosmosis in the guard cells, Uptake of $\text{K}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ ions by guard cells.
Conversion of startch to sugar in guard cells, Formation of Potassium malate in the guard cells, Endosmosis in the guard cells, Uptake of $\text{K}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ ions by guard cells.

Conversion of startch to sugar in guard cells, Formation of Potassium malate in the guard cells, Exosmosis in the guard cells, Prevention of uptake of $\text{K}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ ions by guard cells.

Conversion of sugar to startch in guard cells, Formation of Potassium malate in the guard cells, Exosmosis in the guard cells, Prevention of uptake of $\text{K}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ ions by guard cells.
71550.sol:
The opening of stomata is an active process that depends on the turgidity of the guard cells. According to the active potassium ion transport theory, during the day, starch is converted into malic acid, which dissociates into malate and $\text{H}^+$ ions.

The $\text{H}^+$ ions are actively pumped out of the guard cells, and $\text{K}^+$ ions are taken in from the surrounding subsidiary cells. $\text{Cl}^-$ ions are also taken up to maintain electrical neutrality. The $\text{K}^+$ ions combine with malate to form potassium malate.

The accumulation of potassium malate and the conversion of starch to sugar increase the osmotic concentration inside the guard cells. This causes water to move into the guard cells from the surrounding cells (endosmosis). As a result, the guard cells become turgid, their outer thin walls bulge outward, and the inner thick walls are pulled apart, leading to the opening of the stomatal pore.

Answer: Conversion of startch to sugar in guard cells, Formation of Potassium malate in the guard cells, Endosmosis in the guard cells, Uptake of $\text{K}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ ions by guard cells.

71809.subject: Chemistry
71809.text: Which of the following is heterocyclic aromatic compound?
71809.sol:
A compound is considered aromatic if it is cyclic, planar, completely conjugated, and satisfies Hückel's rule by having $(4n + 2)\pi$ electrons.

Let us examine each option:

Option (1): The structure is a pyrylium ion. It is a six-membered heterocyclic ring containing an oxygen atom. The oxygen atom carries a positive charge and is $sp^2$ hybridized. There are three double bonds in the ring, contributing $6\pi$ electrons. The molecule is cyclic, planar, fully conjugated, and has $6\pi$ electrons (n=1$ in Hückel's rule). Therefore, it is a heterocyclic aromatic compound.

Option (2): The structure is tetrahydropyran. It is a heterocyclic compound but lacks any double bonds. It is non-planar and not conjugated. Therefore, it is non-aromatic.

Option (3): The structure is 4H$-pyran. It contains two double bonds (4\pi$ electrons). One of the carbon atoms in the ring is $sp^3$ hybridized, breaking the continuous conjugation. Therefore, it is non-aromatic.

Option (4): The structure is phenol. It consists of a benzene ring with a hydroxyl group attached. The ring is carbocyclic (containing only carbon atoms in the ring), not heterocyclic. While phenol is an aromatic compound, it is not a heterocyclic aromatic compound. Answer :$

72170.subject: Physics
72170.text: Two coils have mutual inductance of $0.004\ \text{H}$. The current changes in the first coil according to the relation $i = i_0\cos\omega t$, where $i_0 = 6\ \text{A}$ and $\omega = 100\pi\ \text{rad/s}$. The maximum value of emf induced in second coil is
72170.sol:
The induced emf in the second coil is given by $e = -M \dfrac{di}{dt}$.

Given $i = i_0\cos\omega t$, differentiating with respect to time gives $\dfrac{di}{dt} = -i_0\omega\sin\omega t$.

Substituting this into the emf equation gives $e = M i_0\omega\sin\omega t$.

The maximum value of the induced emf is $e_{\text\max} = M i_0\omega$.

Substituting the given values $M = 0.004\ \text{H}$, $i_0 = 6\ \text{A}$, and $\omega = 100\pi\ \text{rad/s}$:

$e_{\text\max} = 0.004 \times 6 \times 100\pi = 2.4\pi\ \text{V}$.

Answer: $2.4\pi\ V$

72336.text: A simple pendulum having length $l$ and mass 'm' is suspended between two plates having uniform electric field 'E' as shown in figure. The bob is given a charge $q$. The time period 'T' of its vibration is
72336.sol:
The forces acting on the bob of the pendulum are the gravitational force $mg$ acting downwards and the electrostatic force $qE$ acting downwards (since the electric field $E$ is directed downwards and the charge $q$ is assumed positive).

The net downward force on the bob is $F_{net} = mg + qE$.

The effective acceleration due to gravity is $g_{eff} = \dfrac{F_{net}}{m} = g + \dfrac{qE}{m}$.

The time period of a simple pendulum is given by $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g_{eff}}}$.

Substituting the value of $g_{eff}$, we get $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g + \dfrac{qE}{m}}}$.

Answer: $2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g + \dfrac{Eq}{m}}}$

72467.subject: Physics
72467.text: A ray of light from a monochromatic point source of light is incident at a point on the screen. If a thin mica film of thickeness 't' and refractive index 'n' is introduced in its path, then the optical path
72467.sol:
Let the original geometric path length be $x$.

Before the introduction of the mica film, the optical path is $x$ (assuming the medium is air or vacuum with refractive index $1$).

When a mica film of thickness $t$ and refractive index $n$ is introduced, the light travels a distance $x - t$ in air and a distance $t$ in the mica film.

The new optical path is $(x - t) \times 1 + t \times n = x + (n - 1)t$.

The change in the optical path is $(x + (n - 1)t) - x = (n - 1)t$.

Thus, the optical path is increased by $(n - 1)t$.

Answer: is increased by (n-1) t.

77849.subject: Mathematics
77849.text:
Passage: A 4-digit number is selected at random formed by using the digits $0$, $1$, $2$, $3$ and $4$ (where repetition of digits is not allowed).

Question: What is the probability that the number selected is divisible by $4$ ?
77849.sol:
Total number of $4$-digit numbers formed using $0, 1, 2, 3, 4$ without repetition:

The thousands place can be filled in $4$ ways (excluding $0$).

The remaining $3$ places can be filled in ^{4}P_{3} = 24$ ways.

Total possible numbers = 4 \times 24 = 96$.

A number is divisible by $4$ if the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by $4$.

The possible last two digits from the given set are $04, 12, 20, 24, 32, 40$.

Case 1: Last two digits are $04, 20$, or $40$ ($3$ cases).

Since $0$ is used, the first two places can be filled from the remaining $3$ digits in ^{3}P_{2} = 6$ ways.

Number of such numbers = 3 \times 6 = 18$.

Case 2: Last two digits are $12, 24$, or $32$ ($3$ cases).

Since $0$ is not used in the last two digits, the thousands place cannot be $0$. It can be filled in $2$ ways.

The hundreds place can be filled in $2$ ways.

Number of such numbers = $3 \times (2 \times 2) = 12$.

Total numbers divisible by $4 = 18 + 12 = 30$.

Required probability = $\dfrac{30}{96} = \dfrac{5}{16}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{5}{16}$

81181.text: Which one of the following is an ambidentate ligand ?
81181.sol:
An ambidentate ligand is a unidentate ligand that has more than one donor atom but coordinates to the central metal atom or ion through only one donor atom at a time.

Thiocyanate ion ($SCN^{-}$ or $NCS^{-}$) has two donor atoms, sulfur ($S$) and nitrogen ($N$). It can bind to the metal through either the sulfur atom (thiocyanato) or the nitrogen atom (isothiocyanato). Thus, it is an ambidentate ligand.

Ethane-$1,2$-diamine is a bidentate ligand.

Ethylenediaminetetraacetate ion is a hexadentate ligand.

Oxalate is a bidentate ligand.

Answer: Thiocyanate

83334.text: In a concave lens, a ray of light emanating from the object parallel to the principal axis of the lens, after refraction :
options: passes through 2F, which is the radius of curvature of the lens.
appears to diverge from the first principal focus.
emerges parallel to the principal axis.
passes through the second principal focus.
83334.sol:
According to the rules of refraction for spherical lenses, a ray of light parallel to the principal axis of a concave lens diverges after refraction.

When this refracted ray is extended backwards, it appears to diverge from the principal focus located on the same side of the lens as the object.

By standard convention, the principal focus on the object side (left side) is termed the first principal focus ($F_1$).

Thus, the ray appears to diverge from the first principal focus.

Answer: appears to diverge from the first principal focus.

85624.subject: Biology
85624.text:
A researcher wants to insert a linear DNA fragment into a plasmid DNA. The linear DNA fragment has two MfeI restriction sites at its ends. The plasmid DNA has only one EcoRI restriction site. The plasmid was digested with EcoRI and the DNA fragment was digested with MfeI. The recognition sequences of the restriction enzymes on one strand are given.
EcoRI site: $5'\text{-G} \downarrow \text{AATTC-}3'$
MfeI site: $5'\text{-C} \downarrow \text{AATTG-}3'$
(arrow indicates enzyme cut sites)
Based on this information, the DNA fragments generated by EcoRI and MfeI
options: cannot ligate to each other because the overhangs generated are from two different enzymes.
can ligate to each other, but the resultant product can neither be digested by EcoRI nor MfeI.
can ligate to each other, and the resultant product can be digested by EcoRI but not MfeI.
can ligate to each other, and the resultant product can be digested by MfeI but not EcoRI.
85624.sol:
The restriction enzyme EcoRI recognizes the sequence $5'\text{-GAATTC-}3'$ and cuts between G and A, generating a $5'\text{-AATT-}3'$ sticky end.

The restriction enzyme MfeI recognizes the sequence $5'\text{-CAATTG-}3'$ and cuts between C and A, also generating a $5'\text{-AATT-}3'$ sticky end.

Since both enzymes produce identical $5'\text{-AATT-}3'$ overhangs, the DNA fragments have compatible sticky ends and can successfully ligate to each other.

When the fragments ligate, the junctions formed will be a combination of the half-sites from each enzyme:
Ligating the EcoRI left half-site ($5'\text{-G-}3'$) with the MfeI right half-site ($5'\text{-AATTG-}3'$) produces the sequence $5'\text{-GAATTG-}3'$.
Ligating the MfeI left half-site ($5'\text{-C-}3'$) with the EcoRI right half-site ($5'\text{-AATTC-}3'$) produces the sequence $5'\text{-CAATTC-}3'$.

The newly formed junction sequences are $5'\text{-GAATTG-}3'$ and $5'\text{-CAATTC-}3'$. Neither of these sequences matches the recognition site for EcoRI ($5'\text{-GAATTC-}3'$) or MfeI ($5'\text{-CAATTG-}3'$).

Therefore, the fragments can ligate to each other, but the resultant product can neither be digested by EcoRI nor MfeI.

Answer: can ligate to each other, but the resultant product can neither be digested by EcoRI nor MfeI.

So \left|$ sin (x + T )\right| + $\left|$ cos (x + T )\right| = $\left|$ sinx\right| + $\left|$ cosx\right| .$

Squaring both sides, we get,

1 + \left|$ sin ( 2x + 2T )\right| = 1 + $\left|$ sin2x\right|$

Therefore, the fundamental period of \left|$ sinx\right| + $\left|$ cosx\right|$ is& \dfrac{\pi}{2}

Hence, \dfrac{2\pi}{a} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}

$⇒ a = 4$$

91364.text: Let $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ be three real numbers satisfying $\left[\alpha\beta\gamma\right]\left[\begin{cases}2 & - 1 & 1 \\ - 1 & - 1 & - 2 \\ - 1 & 2 & 1\end{cases}\right]$ =$\left[000\right]$. $\left[\alpha\beta\gamma\right]\left[\begin{cases}2 & - 1 & 1 \\ - 1 & - 1 & - 2 \\ - 1 & 2 & 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[000\right]$
$\left[\begin{cases}2\alpha - \beta - \gamma & - \alpha - \beta + 2\gamma & \alpha - 2\beta + \gamma\end{cases}\right] = \left[000\right]$
$⇒ 2\alpha - \beta - \gamma = 0$
$- \alpha - \beta + 2\gamma = 0$
$\alpha - 2\beta + \gamma = 0$
Using cramer’s rule
$∆ = \left|\begin{cases}2 & - 1 & - 1 \\ - 1 & - 1 & 2 \\ 1 & - 2 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 2\left(- 1 + 4\right) + 1\left(- 1 - 2\right) - 1\left(2 + 1\right)$
$= 6 - 3 - 3 = 0$
So, the system of equations has infinite solutions
Put $\gamma = k$
$\left\begin{array}{ll}2\alpha - \beta = k \\ \alpha + \beta = 2k\end{array}\right\} ⇒ \gamma = k, \beta = k$
$⇒ \left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right) ≡ \left(k, k, k\right)$
$∵ \left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$ satisfies $2x + y + 3z = 2$
$⇒ 6k = 2 ⇒ k = \dfrac{1}{3}$
$\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right) ≡ \left(\dfrac{1}{3}, \dfrac{1}{3}, \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$
$⇒ 3\alpha + 2\beta - 6\gamma = - \dfrac{1}{3}$
